subject: ChatFlow MAP: performance benchmarks, TTFT & streaming latency — proposed execution
messages:
From: Dan Hughes <dan.hughes@chatflow.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Nov 2027 15:08:00 -0800
Subject: Request: MAP + performance targets for streaming chat (TTFT, p50/p95/p99)

Diego / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the model latency you showed looked promising. Procurement and our infra team asked for a Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that includes precise benchmarking targets and an execution timeline before they greenlight pilots.

Specifically we need:
- TTFT (time-to-first-token) for streaming chat under expected concurrency (1, 8, 32, 64)
- Streaming latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) for 1k / 2k token windows and 1-shot vs few-shot prompts
- Sustained throughput (tokens/s) and observed tail behaviour under concurrency ramps
- A short MAP with milestones, deliverables, and acceptance criteria we can share with our security/procurement folks

Can Redwood produce the MAP + a small results dump (logs and a short summary) by end of next week? If you already have a template that maps to these metrics that’d speed things up.

Also looping in procurement: procurement@chatflow.ai — they’ll be the signer for the PoC contract.

Cheers,
Dan Hughes
VP Engineering, ChatFlow Labs
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Request: MAP + performance targets for streaming chat (TTFT, p50/p95/p99)

Team — putting together an execution plan for ChatFlow (see bullets). Quick assignments so we can hit Dan's end-of-week ask: 

1) Marissa — lead the MAP doc and coordinate sign-off. Draft the MAP skeleton (deliverables/milestones/acceptance criteria) and share with Dan for approval. Target: draft by Wed EOD 11/30. Attachment: MAP-action-items.docx (stub).
2) Vanessa — run the streaming TTFT sweep across quantization profiles they care about (float16, q4_0) at concurrencies: 1, 8, 32, 64. Produce p50/p95/p99 for 1k and 2k token windows and capture perf-logs-20271130.tar.gz. Target: initial run by Tue 11/30 morning.
3) Connor — prepare the methodology workbook for transparency (bench-methodology.xlsx). Include traffic shaping, prompt templates, and KV-cache warm/cold scenarios.

Notes on acceptance criteria (proposed):
- TTFT <= 200ms at concurrency 1 (p50) for 1k prompt; p95 < 420ms; p99 < 700ms
- Streaming p95 under 600ms at concurrency 8 for our recommended config
- No >5% error/timeout rate during 30-minute sustained run at concurrency 32

I'll own the MAP PDF and the external write-up. Marissa — once you have the draft, I’ll merge the bench summary and send to Dan.

Diego
Diego Fernandez
Head, Solutions Architecture | Redwood Inference
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Dan Hughes <dan.hughes@chatflow.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Nov 2027 13:45:00 -0800
Subject: ChatFlow MAP & benchmark summary (initial results)

Dan — attached is our proposed MAP and the first-pass benchmark summary. We ran controlled streaming sweeps and captured TTFT and tail percentiles; details below and attachments are included.

Attachments: ChatFlow_MAP_v1.pdf (MAP with milestones), bench-methodology.xlsx, perf-logs-20271130.tar.gz

Executive summary (short):
- Method: 30-minute sustained streams using your 1-shot prompt template and a 1k token response target. Sessions ramped to target concurrency and held steady; KV-cache warmed after initial prefix.
- TTFT (median / p95 / p99):
  - Concurrency 1: 140ms / 360ms / 610ms
  - Concurrency 8: 165ms / 480ms / 820ms
  - Concurrency 32: 220ms / 640ms / 1200ms
  - Concurrency 64: 360ms / 980ms / 2100ms (observed backpressure; recommend burst policy for production)
- Streaming payload latency (per token tail behaviour): p50 < 30ms, p95 up to 120ms at high concurrency; p99 spikes during GC/eviction windows — logs attached
- Throughput: sustained ~1.2k tokens/s at concurrency 32 on our dedicated config; throughput drops as backpressure increases at >32 if not using batching adjustments.

Proposed MAP milestones (high level):
1) Sign MAP (DocuSign link included) — target 7 calendar days
2) Run expanded acceptance bench (our infra + your sample traffic) — 3 business days
3) Joint validation and acceptance call — 1 business day
4) Pilot roll (2 weeks) with instrumentation and fallback policy

Acceptance criteria (from our draft): TTFT p95 <= 500ms at concurrency 8 for your 1k target; sustained error rate <2% in 30-minute window.

Next steps: Marissa will follow up with the MAP PDF and DocuSign. If the numbers look reasonable, can we schedule the joint validation call Thu 12/2 or Fri 12/3?

Thanks — Diego
From: Dan Hughes <dan.hughes@chatflow.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@chatflow.ai
Date: Wed, 1 Dec 2027 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ChatFlow MAP & benchmark summary (initial results)

Diego / team — this is helpful, thanks. The TTFT/p95 numbers for concurrencies 1 and 8 look compatible with our requirements; we have concerns at the 64-concurrency tail but we can accept a burst/fallback strategy during pilot.

Procurement is ready to review the MAP — please send the DocuSign and the MAP PDF. Also please include the bench-methodology.xlsx so our infra team can validate the approach.

We can do Thu 12/2 11:00am PT for the joint validation call. I’ll send a calendar invite once I confirm with my manager.

— Dan
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Dan Hughes <dan.hughes@chatflow.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>, procurement@chatflow.ai
Date: Wed, 1 Dec 2027 17:05:00 -0800
Subject: RE: ChatFlow MAP & benchmark summary (initial results)

Perfect — moving forward. Marissa will send the DocuSign and MAP PDF now (you should see it within the hour). Vanessa will prepare an expanded acceptance run that exercises your spike profile and will drop the detailed perf logs in the shared Drive. Connor will join the call on Thu 12/2 at 11:00am PT.

Quick note for the call: we’ll bring:
- A short slide (1 page) showing TTFT / p95 breakouts by concurrency and quantization profile
- The bench-methodology workbook for transparency
- A live look at the streaming traces (if time permits)

Diego
Head, Solutions Architecture | Redwood Inference
Attachments referenced: ChatFlow_MAP_v1.pdf, bench-methodology.xlsx, perf-logs-20271130.tar.gz
